title: Rapid 3D phenotypic analysis of neurons and organoids using data-driven cell segmentation-free machine learning
summary: Phindr3D combines unsupervised k-means voxel features with hierarchical supervoxel and megavoxel descriptors for segmentation-free 3D image phenotyping. In 8,100 neuronal image stacks across 9 biological replicates, it separated treatment-associated morphologies, including distinct responses to anti-apoptotic inhibitors, and it characterized oncogene-associated morphogenesis in mammary acinar organoids. These assay-bound results do not establish clinical utility.
ai_technology: Phindr3D shallow-learning pipeline: unsupervised k-means voxel categories, hierarchical supervoxel/megavoxel features, affinity-propagation clustering, and random-forest classification
organization: Sunnybrook Research Institute, University of Toronto

evidence.tested: The tool processed 8,100 three-channel neuronal image stacks from 9 biological replicates on 3 plates; affinity-propagation clustering yielded eight combined phenotype clusters and separated responses to anti-apoptotic inhibitors with similar profiles across replicates. In a reference 3D cell-line assay, concentration-response EC50 values were similar to conventional segmentation-based classification.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is limited to the reported microscopy assays and models; generalization to other imaging tasks and clinical utility were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Phindr3D derives hierarchical voxel-based image features without cell segmentation; unsupervised k-means builds pixel, supervoxel, and megavoxel categories, followed by affinity-propagation clustering or random-forest classification.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
